units: USD millions unless noted; percentages are year-over-year growth as stated by Kroger
conventions: Each quarter's figures come from that quarter's own Item 2.02 earnings release (EX-99.1), as first reported. total_sales_musd and net_earnings_musd (net earnings attributable to The Kroger Co.; negative = loss) are from Table 1. identical_sales_ex_fuel_pct and adjusted_eps_usd are the headline figures. ecommerce_sales_growth_pct is whatever online-sales growth the release states; ecommerce_metric_reported names the measure because Kroger switched from 'digital sales' (FY2024) to 'eCommerce sales' (Q1-Q3 FY2025) to 'adjusted eCommerce sales' (Q4 FY2025 on). Kroger does not disclose quarterly eCommerce dollar sales, so ecommerce_sales_musd is null throughout. weeks follows Kroger's fiscal calendar (Q1 = 16 weeks, Q2-Q4 = 12 weeks in a 52-week year), stated explicitly in the FY2026 10-Qs. No customer metric (loyal households, Boost members, pharmacy) is reported with a number in most quarters, so none gets its own key; FY2024 qualitative mentions are quoted in notes.

deal.assumed_wording: 8-K: "approximately $400 million in assumed liabilities"; 10-Q: "approximately $400 million in assumed indebtedness"
deal.expected_close_wording: 8-K: "expected to close in 2027"; 10-Q: "expected to close in fiscal year 2027"
deal.divestitures: Kroger and Giant Eagle expect to make limited Giant Eagle store divestitures

other_mentions.what: Investor Update release: long-term targets footnoted "Excludes the pending acquisition of Giant Eagle."

deal.not_disclosed: No Giant Eagle revenue, earnings, store count, banner plans, app or loyalty (myPerks) plans in any Kroger filing reviewed.

quarters.notes: Release says "Grew digital sales more than 8%, with Delivery and Pickup combining for double-digit growth" (8 is a floor). Also "Increased delivery sales by 17% over last year led by Customer Fulfillment Centers", "Increased digitally engaged households by 9% compared to last year" and "Increased total households, loyal households and customer visits" (no household counts given). Net earnings = net earnings attributable to The Kroger Co. (Table 1).

Release says "Grew digital sales 11%". Also "Increased delivery sales by 17% over last year led by Customer Fulfillment Centers", "Grew eCommerce households by 14% compared to last year", "Increased total households, customer visits and loyal households" (no counts), and "Held Boost Bonus Days, a two-week mega-sales event with exclusive access for Boost by Kroger Plus members".

Release says "Grew digital sales 11%". Also "Increased delivery sales by 18% over last year led by Customer Fulfillment Centers", "Our Brands sales growth outpaced total grocery sales growth", "Increased total households and loyal households" (no counts), and "Enhanced the Boost by Kroger Plus Membership by including Disney streaming options with an annual membership". Kroger Specialty Pharmacy sale closed this quarter (affects later year-over-year sales comparisons).

Release says "Delivered 11% digital sales growth, excluding the 53rd week in 2023" and "Increased delivery sales by 18% over last year, excluding the 53rd week in 2023, led by Customer Fulfillment Centers". The prior-year quarter included the 53rd week of fiscal 2023, so headline year-over-year comparisons are distorted; Kroger's growth figures here exclude it. Last release to report delivery sales growth. Households are not mentioned.

Release says "eCommerce sales increased 15%". Wording switches from "digital sales" to "eCommerce sales" this quarter, so the series is not like-for-like across the switch. Identical sales excludes adjustment items (Colorado labor dispute). Release stops reporting households and delivery growth.
Release says "eCommerce sales increased 16%". CFO: sales growth "led by pharmacy, eCommerce and Fresh".

Release says "eCommerce sales increased 17%". Net loss includes "$2.6 billion in previously announced impairment and related charges ($3.00 loss per share) for automated fulfillment network". CEO: "We have now completed our strategic review which we expect will make our eCommerce business profitable in 2026."

Release says "Adjusted eCommerce sales1 increased 20%" (the 1 is a footnote marker; footnote: adjusted eCommerce sales "exclude the effect of fulfillment center exits in markets where Kroger does not operate stores, the sale of Vitacost, and the discontinuation of Ship Marketplace"). First quarter on the adjusted basis, not comparable to earlier quarters. Identical sales includes an unfavorable 38 bp Inflation Reduction Act impact.

Release says "Adjusted eCommerce sales grew +19%" and "Kroger Precision Marketing profit grew over 20%". The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926078236/kr-20260523x10q.htm) gives the unadjusted figure: "eCommerce sales increased 13% in the first quarter of 2026", and says "Our eCommerce business, including Media, was profitable this quarter." Identical sales includes an unfavorable 130 bp Inflation Reduction Act impact. 16 weeks per the 10-Q ("16-week periods").

Release says "Adjusted eCommerce sales grew +20%" and "Kroger Precision Marketing profit grew +24%". The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926108926/kr-20260815x10q.htm) gives the unadjusted figure: "eCommerce sales increased 14% in the second quarter", growth "led by increased demand for Delivery solutions", and "Our eCommerce business, including third-party media revenue, was profitable in the second quarter". Identical sales includes an unfavorable 138 bp Inflation Reduction Act impact. FY2026 identical sales guidance cut to 0.2% - 0.8%. Release does not mention Giant Eagle; the 10-Q does (note 10).

annual.ecommerce_sales_stated: Delivered more than $13B in digital sales
annual.notes: Total sales from Table 1 (year-to-date). Includes $2,021M of Kroger Specialty Pharmacy sales (per FY2025 10-K). Digital sales stated only as a floor. Growth figure (11%) is from the FY2025 10-K sales table footnote: "eCommerce sales increased 16% in 2025, 11% in 2024".

annual.ecommerce_sales_stated: Delivered more than $16 billion in eCommerce sales
annual.notes: Total sales from Table 1 (year-to-date). eCommerce dollars stated only as a floor. Growth from the FY2025 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/56873/000110465926037723/kr-20260131x10k.htm): "eCommerce sales increased 16% compared to 2024"; 17% excluding fulfillment center exits, Vitacost.com and Ship Marketplace. Release also: "Completed eCommerce strategic review, which is expected to deliver $400 million in eCommerce operating profit improvement in 2026".

latest_quarter_available: Q2 FY2026 (ended 2026-08-15). Q3 FY2026 not yet reported as of 2026-10-20.
